title: How to Automate Pixtral Large 2502 Vision Workflows
summary: To automate Pixtral Large 2502, developers can integrate API endpoints into existing image processing pipelines to scale complex visual analysis tasks.
body_markdown:
## Multimodal automation with Pixtral Large 2502


### Hardware requirements for local vs. managed analysis


Mistral’s analysis puts the local deployment requirement for a 123B parameter model at high-memory GPU clusters. This prevents out-of-memory (OOM) crashes during the long-context vision encoding phase.


### Pixtral Large 2502 VRAM requirements


This typically necessitates a cluster of four A100 80GB GPUs to accommodate the weights and the KV cache, effectively limiting accessibility to organizations with significant infrastructure budgets.


For teams utilizing 4-bit quantization to reduce the memory footprint, the requirement drops to approximately 150GB of VRAM, so the model becomes viable on slightly more modest server setups.


This allows for deployment on a dual A100 80GB configuration, though performance may vary during peak visual encoding, meaning users should anticipate potential latency spikes during complex image processing tasks.


For teams lacking dedicated H100 or A100 infrastructure, the Mistral La Plateforme API handles the VRAM requirements for image processing on Mistral’s managed infrastructure.


This shift from local weights to managed endpoints allows developers to focus on the logic of the vision request rather than the thermal throttling of a local server rack.


### Getting your Mistral API key


Automated workflows depend on a Mistral La Plateforme API Key to authenticate requests and track usage against account limits.


Without a valid key, the automation engine will return a 401 Unauthorized error, stalling the entire data pipeline. To begin, ensure your environment meets the following technical baseline:


The environment requires a Mistral La Plateforme API Key and a Python 3.11+ environment. You also need a public URL or Base64 string for image hosting.


Establishing this environment ensures that the script has the necessary libraries and permissions to transmit visual data to the 2502 model.


### Preparing image URLs for vision processing


Pixtral Large 2502 requires images accessible via a public URL. You can also encode them as a Base64 string within the JSON payload.


If a firewall or a local drive without a gateway stores an image, the model will return a "Failed to fetch image" error.


This results in an empty response for the visual reasoning step. Validating that your hosting provider allows external GET requests from Mistral’s IP ranges is the final prerequisite before initiating a multimodal call.
